verdict.rationale: First-party docs describe running Claude Code on the web in cloud sessions with no local setup. You can kick off long-running tasks, check back when they're done, run several in parallel, and later pull a session into your terminal with `claude --teleport`. That covers background delegation to a remote cloud environment. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of how the cloud environment is isolated or sandboxed (the Bash sandbox doc covers local execution only), and independent or hands-on corroboration of cloud background runs.

support.subject: As a developer, I can delegate longer-running coding tasks to run in the background in an isolated cloud environment

citations.quote: Run Claude Code in your browser with no local setup. Kick off long-running tasks and check back when they're done, work on repos you don't have locally, or run multiple tasks in parallel.
Kick off a long-running task on the web or the Claude mobile app, then pull it into your terminal with `claude --teleport`.
schedule recurring tasks, and kick off cloud sessions.
